- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.08) in recent days, model tends to under-forecast; adjust forecast upward by 0.5–1.5% of recent mean or spike magnitude.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.22), model often over-forecasts; reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% to align with mean reversion bias.
- Model consistently over-estimates early in 30-day horizon after sharp price spikes (e.g., +5–10% overshoot); apply lag correction by subtracting 1–2% of spike magnitude.
- Model under-estimates mean-reverting periods (e.g., after 65–68 range) — increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% to capture momentum toward higher mean.
- If sentiment is neutral (0.00–0.08) and price is trending upward, model lags; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to capture momentum.
- If sentiment is neutral and price is trending downward, model over-estimates; reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% to avoid overcorrection.
- Model tends to underestimate 30-day horizon when sentiment is volatile (±0.17 or higher) — add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to account for sentiment-driven volatility.
